name: Madeleine
origin: A small shell-shaped sponge cake from Commercy, Lorraine, made famous by Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time; the classic 'hump' on its back is produced by baking at a high initial heat, a real thermal-shock effect.

process.name: whisk eggs and sugar
process.description: whisk whole eggs and sugar until pale and thick

process.name: fold in dry and butter
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and zest, then melted butter

process.name: chill batter
process.description: chill the batter, a real technique for a sharper, more reliable hump when the cold batter hits a hot mould

notes: Ratios follow the standard madeleine proportion documented across French patisserie references (a rich, buttery genoise-adjacent batter, closer to a small butter cake than to a lean sponge). Chilling the batter before a hot bake is real, standard technique for producing the characteristic hump, and is included as a process step rather than a formulation detail.
